Question: A triangle \(ABC\) is to be constructed given side \(a\) (opposite angle \(A\)), angle \(B,\) and \(h_c,\) the altitude from \(C.\) If \(N\) is the number of noncongruent solutions, then \(N\)
Solution:
The altitude from \(C\) measures its perpendicular distance to the entire line \(AB\), including an extension of the side. This distance does not depend on how far \(A\) lies along its ray from \(B\).

A nondegenerate triangle requires \(a>0\), \(h_c>0\), and \(0<B<180^\circ\); data failing these requirements give no solution. For valid side and angle data, fix \(BC=a\), and draw a ray from \(B\) making the given angle \(B\) with \(BC\). Every candidate triangle can be placed in this position, reflecting it if necessary. Let \(d>0\) be the distance from \(C\) to the line containing that ray.

If \(h_c\ne d\), no choice of \(A\) can give the required altitude, so \(N=0\).

If \(h_c=d\), every point \(A\ne B\) on the ray gives a nondegenerate triangle satisfying the data. To prove that infinitely many are noncongruent, choose \(A_n\) with
\[
BA_n=na,\qquad n=1,2,3,\ldots.
\]
Their areas are
\[
\frac12(BA_n)h_c=\frac{na h_c}{2}.
\]
These areas are distinct because \(a,h_c>0\), and congruent triangles have equal areas. Thus this case gives infinitely many noncongruent triangles. Therefore \(N\) must be zero or infinite, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
